header.target: PR #48 screenshot support in problem briefs
header.round_context: Mode: design review of the PR's approach, not a line-by-line diff review. PR #48 (branch worktree-fix-46-47-visuals, draft, closes issues #46 and #47) adds screenshot support to problem briefs. Deltas: (1) schema/problem-brief.schema.json — new diagram kind "image" (PNG/JPEG/WebP, required alt + caption, optional fileDark) and an optional "image" object on evidence items; (2) bin/validate-brief.mjs — checkImage() refuses missing/non-raster/>1 MB pictures when given a baseDir, warns above 6 MB total, and warns when a live entry's prose or evidence mentions .html/.png/.svg/mockup/screenshot and carries no image or svg; validateBrief gains a third baseDir parameter; (3) bin/render-brief.mjs — shot() embeds pictures as base64 data URIs inside a <button class="shot">, images grouped in a wrapping .shots row, a click toggles .zoom, dark/light swap by CSS; (4) bin/brief.mjs — --diagram list flag on raise and set (set appends to unwound.diagrams), validation now receives the brief's folder; (5) bin/extract-brief.mjs — writes embedded pictures back to files beside the recovered JSON, refusing paths that climb out of that folder; (6) SKILL.md, reference/entry-format.md, reference/diagrams.md, README.md — rule: show the reader what they must see; a path or markup line is not evidence for a visual question. Not done: no image resizing (zero-dependency scripts). Tests: 104 pass incl. 4 new. Zero-dependency Node 18+ project; no Python. No prior chorus record exists.

questions.question: Which quality matters most for problem-brief: (a) the operator can answer an entry from the published page alone, often on a phone; (b) the brief's JSON can be rebuilt from its published page; (c) zero dependencies and portable scripts; (d) the JSON stays readable and diffable?
questions.answer: Readable page first: (a) page answerable on a phone > (b) recovery > (c) zero dependencies > (d) diffable JSON.

questions.question: Who should the reviewers judge problem-brief as being built for: one operator, or public users through install.sh?
questions.answer: Public users: a tool shipped publicly through install.sh, used by people other than the author.

questions.question: On a phone, when you tap a screenshot in a brief, what should happen? The PR shows it at true pixel size with sideways scrolling.
questions.answer: Fit, pinch to zoom: keep it fitted to the screen width; open it fitted in a full-screen view where you pinch to zoom.

questions.question: Should an evidence screenshot have its own required caption, as issue #47 asked? The PR uses the evidence note as the caption.
questions.answer: Note is caption: keep the PR's choice; the evidence note already says what the picture shows.

questions.question: Does a typical session have any way to resize an image before the 1 MB refusal?
How often do live entries mention 'screenshot' or '.png' with no visual question behind them?
Does the artifact frame let the click toggle and the page's horizontal scroll work on a phone?
Is refusing a bad screenshot at validation while degrading a bad svg/archify drawing to a note at render time a deliberate split?
Is the data-brief-file markup that extract-brief parses a stable contract between render and extract, or an internal detail?
Does the project expect test-first, or only that a test lands with the change?
Is git show HEAD the intended scope, given local main is behind the PR's parent?
Issue #47 asked for a warning when the rendered page passes 8 MB; the PR warns when raw image bytes pass 6 MB. Was that change deliberate?

findings.claim: A picture over 1 MB is refused, and because brief.mjs refuses the whole command on any fresh error, the entry is never raised: the operator's question disappears along with the picture. The hint tells the author to resize to 1600px, but the PR ships no resizer and the docs name none (reference/diagrams.md:49 'The renderer does not resize'; :50 names only Chrome for capture). A full-page retina PNG passes 1 MB easily. Bedrock: zero dependencies (ranked c) is beating answering from the page (ranked a). Recovery needs no new dependency: document a capture recipe that fits (set Chrome width, save as JPEG or WebP), or degrade (raise the entry, warn, show a 'picture too large' note). Which one is the operator's call; the mechanism goes to Richards and Norman. Assumption: no resizing tool exists in a session (ruled deferred).

evidence.note: hard refusal, hint asks for a resize
any fresh error refuses the whole raise/set
renderer does not resize; capture via Chrome only

findings.pull_quote: A screenshot over 1 MB doesn't only lose the picture: the operator's question never gets raised, and the fix the hint asks for needs a tool nobody shipped.

findings.claim: Tapping a screenshot sets max-width:none inside a horizontally scrolling button. On a phone, 'full size' then means a 1600px picture panned sideways inside a 360px frame, and another tap closes it again. This is the top-ranked path (operator on a phone), and the operator has already ruled the opposite behaviour: fitted, full-screen, pinch-zoom. Because it sits on quality (a), I would land the ruled behaviour before merge rather than in a follow-up. Mechanism goes to Norman; behaviour in the artifact frame is unverified (deferred).
findings.pull_quote: On a phone, tapping a screenshot to see it better makes it worse: a wide picture you scroll sideways through a narrow slot, the opposite of what the operator ruled.

findings.claim: Any svg drawing counts as 'shown', so an entry with an unrelated architecture svg plus a path to an HTML mockup gets no warning. That is the #46 case with one extra drawing. The other way round, a public user's ordinary web-code citation ('src/index.html:42' for a non-visual bug) fires the warning. The test covers only the plain #46 case and a .mjs citation (test/brief.test.mjs:1198-1202), so neither edge is pinned. A warning that misses its own case and cries wolf on web projects teaches authors to ignore it. Count an svg as shown only when it is the visual in question, or drop svg from 'shown' and let a noDiagram-style line silence it.
findings.pull_quote: The warning stays quiet on the #46 case as soon as the entry also carries any svg, and it fires on every honest code citation of an .html file.

findings.claim: Extract writes each embedded picture over whatever file has that name beside the output JSON, with no check and no notice. Someone rebuilding a brief from a page into their own folder (quality b, public users) can silently lose their own shots/q2-wide.png to the page's copy. The escape check guards the folder but not the files inside it. User cost: lost local pictures with no warning. Mechanism (skip, refuse or --force) goes to Richards and Uncle Bob.

evidence.note: path-escape refused; existing file overwritten unconditionally

findings.pull_quote: Recovering a brief from a page can quietly overwrite the screenshots already sitting in your folder, and nothing tells you it happened.

findings.claim: F-UV (user-value strip). Named outcome: the operator answers a visual entry from the published page alone. v1 after deferrals: images embedded (Full), alt and caption (Full), several per entry (Full), theme pair (Full), phone zoom (Partial, F2), page weight controlled by resizing (None: refuse only, F1). Estimated value ratio ~80%, above the 20% threshold: not delivery theater. Beneficiary of the resize deferral: the zero-dependency rule. Cost: author excise per capture, plus up to ~8 MB of page weight on the operator's mobile data before any warning (validate-brief.mjs:256).
findings.pull_quote: Most of the promise ships; the deferred resizer is paid for by the author on every capture and by the operator's phone data, so price it rather than hide it.

findings.claim: Extract writes whatever path a page names, with whatever bytes it carries, anywhere under the output folder. The only check is the folder escape. The raster-type rule the validator owns (IMAGE_TYPES) is not applied, so a page someone else published can plant .claude/settings.json (hooks), .git/hooks/* or a script beside the recovered JSON. I reproduced this: a page with data-brief-file=".claude/settings.json" wrote that file. The tool ships publicly, and its own comment says 'the page may not be ours'. That makes this a trust boundary, and it needs the type rule. Duplicate-authority ruling: CONSOLIDATE. extract imports IMAGE_TYPES from validate-brief.mjs, which is safe to import because its CLI is guarded by invokedDirectly. Then it refuses any name whose extension is not a picture, any dot-segment, and any overwrite of an existing file. Fitness function: a test that extracts a hostile page and asserts nothing outside a picture extension is written.

evidence.note: Regex accepts any data-brief-file. Only the relative('..') and isAbsolute checks run before writeFileSync.
IMAGE_TYPES is the one picture-type authority. The renderer imports it and extract does not.
Only the happy round trip is tested. No hostile-page or escape-refusal test exists.

findings.pull_quote: Extract trusts a stranger's page to name files, and the picture-type rule never reaches it; I got it to write .claude/settings.json.

findings.claim: One page-weight budget has two authors that cannot see each other. The validator caps each picture at 1 MB and warns at 6 MB of picture bytes. The renderer caps each drawing at 4 MB and warns at a 6 MB page. The 16 MB ceiling is a string literal in both. The validator's 6 MB counts pictures and ignores inlined SVG and archify, while the renderer's counts the whole page after the fact. So a brief can pass the validator's budget and still break the real constraint, or trip two different warnings for one cause. Ruling: CONSOLIDATE into validate-brief.mjs. The renderer already imports from it, they ship as one unit and one runtime, and the new coupling point costs nothing. Fitness function: a test asserting the renderer holds no byte-limit constants of its own.

evidence.note: INLINE_MAX 4 MB and PAGE_WARN 6 MB, the renderer's copy.
IMAGE_MAX 1 MB and IMAGES_WARN 6 MB, the validator's copy.
The 16 MB literal again, counting picture bytes only.

findings.pull_quote: The page has one size limit and two scripts guessing at it from different numbers; put the budget in the validator the renderer already imports.

findings.claim: The 1 MB per-picture refusal stands in for the real constraint, the 16 MB page. Because brief.mjs refuses the whole write on a fresh error, one 1.2 MB retina phone screenshot blocks the raise. The author's recovery is 'resize or save as JPEG', which needs a tool the session does not have (deferred assumption). The top-ranked quality, answering from the page on a phone, is then lost to a limit the platform does not impose. Better cost profile: warn per picture, refuse only on the total that actually threatens the ceiling.

evidence.note: Any fresh error refuses the command and writes nothing.

findings.pull_quote: A 1 MB hard stop protects against a limit that lives at 16 MB, and the author has no tool to get under it.
findings.need_info_reason: Depends on the deferred assumption that no resizing tool is available in a session, and on how big typical phone screenshots really are.

findings.claim: The render-to-extract seam is a contract written in HTML: attribute order, a data:image/[a-z]+ pattern, and a hand-written inverse of esc(). It has two authors, and nothing calls it a contract. Merging them would mean extract importing render-brief, which runs its CLI at top level, so I rule SANCTIONED DIVERGENCE. Owners: render shot() for the writer, extract for the reader. Reason: extract must stay runnable alone. The round-trip test is the parity detector, but it uses only plain filenames. Extend it with a name that needs escaping, such as an ampersand or quote, so drift fails the build.

evidence.note: The reader decodes by hand, in reverse order, and depends on attribute order.
The existing parity test uses only plain names.

findings.pull_quote: The img markup is a contract with two authors; keep both, but make the round-trip test use a filename that needs escaping so drift goes red.

findings.claim: Picture policy is split across files. The validator owns the type table and the 1 MB cap, and checks the disk only when given a baseDir (validate-brief.mjs:254-285). shot() reads files with no guard and relies on the validator having run. In the same file, the svg/archify path catches a missing or oversized file and degrades to a missingDiagram note under a separate 4 MB cap. So a missing screenshot stops the render while a missing drawing becomes a note. A caller of validateBrief(brief) without baseDir, such as the test helper messages(), passes the check, and shot() then throws ENOENT. Put reading, typing, the size limit and encoding in one place, and choose one failure policy for every drawing kind.

evidence.note: svg/archify catch, then missingDiagram, 4 MB cap

findings.pull_quote: A missing screenshot kills the render, but a missing drawing in the same file degrades to an honest note. One rule, two owners, two outcomes: give pictures one home and one failure policy.

findings.claim: The path-escape refusal guards the trust boundary ('the page may not be ours'), yet no test fails if it is removed. The round-trip test uses only benign paths. Add tests with '../x.png' and with an absolute path that assert nothing is written outside the folder.
findings.pull_quote: The one line that stops a stranger's page from writing outside the folder has no test that fails without it.

findings.claim: extract-brief re-parses shot()'s output with a regex that depends on attribute order, plus a hand-written HTML unescape. If shot() reorders its attributes, every picture is silently dropped on extract. Keep the emitter and the parser together, or share the attribute name as a constant.
findings.pull_quote: Render writes a format and extract re-parses it with a regex in another file. That is a contract with no name, and quality (b) rests on it.
findings.need_info_reason: Whether data-brief-file is a stable contract was deferred; I judged it from the code.

findings.claim: The visual-pointer heuristic adds an authoring-advice job to semanticErrors. Its regex flags any .png, .svg or .html token, so an ordinary citation such as 'src/icons/logo.svg:12' on a live entry warns, and the only negative test uses a .mjs ref. Extract it as a named function with its own false-positive test.
findings.pull_quote: A heuristic with an unknown false-positive rate is sitting inside the structural validator. Name it, test the noisy case, and keep it apart.
findings.need_info_reason: The false-positive rate on real briefs is deferred.

findings.claim: '--diagram appends to unwound.diagrams' is written twice: as an immutable spread in raise and as a mutating push in set. Use one addDiagrams helper.
findings.pull_quote: The append rule for --diagram lives in two places in two shapes. One helper, one rule.

findings.claim: Disk I/O hides behind an optional third positional argument, and every caller passes 'undefined' for schema to reach it. Leave the argument out and the check silently weakens, which is the gap behind F1. Make the effect explicit: an options object ({ baseDir }) or a separate checkPictures(brief, baseDir).
findings.pull_quote: A validator that reads the disk only when you remember a third positional argument hides its effect and fails open when you forget it.

findings.claim: The PR's only trust-boundary refusal has no test. extract-brief skips a picture whose path climbs out of the output folder, and nothing fails if that check is deleted. The page may be someone else's (comment at :40-42), and ruling (b) rests on extract. Why untested? The round trip uses only safe paths, and those come from our own renderer. The risky input is a hand-made page, and no test builds one. Cornering test: HTML with data-brief-file="../evil.png" and an absolute path; assert nothing is written outside the folder and a warning appears. Whether the check is strong enough (symlinks, Windows paths) is another lens's call.
findings.pull_quote: The one refusal between a stranger's page and your disk can be deleted and every test stays green.

findings.claim: The round trip correctly uses two real producers, renderer and extractor, but its fixture is blind in two places. Light and dark are the same bytes, so a swap passes. The paths need no escaping, so drift between esc() and the extractor's decoder is invisible. Fix: different bytes per file, a path containing & or ', and assert both files come back.
findings.pull_quote: The round trip uses one picture for both light and dark, so it would pass with them swapped.

findings.claim: The picture tag is one rule with two authors. shot() and esc() write it; a regex tied to the exact attribute order and a hand-written decoder read it back. They agree today, and only F2's sharper fixture would catch a split. The rule is new and has never moved, so the bet is small. Tidy first, structure-only: export the attribute name and an unescape next to esc(), or have extract read file names from the JSON. Where that seam lives is for architecture.
findings.pull_quote: The renderer writes the picture tag and the extractor parses it back with its own regex and decoder: one rule, two copies.

findings.claim: raise --diagram has its own merge with diagrams passed in --unwound, and no test; only set --diagram is tested. One CLI test passing both, asserting both survive in order, corners it.
findings.pull_quote: set --diagram has a test; raise --diagram has its own merge and none.

findings.claim: The 6 MB warning is the only signal before the 16 MB publish limit, and no test reaches it. Seven sparse 1 MB files would. Threshold judged as written, per the deferred ruling.
findings.pull_quote: The warning that comes before a too-heavy page has never been made to fire.

findings.claim: The validator stat()s a picture and the renderer reads it, so a directory named x.png passes validation and crashes the render. Also, without a baseDir the disk check is skipped silently and missing pictures come back ok. Every bin caller passes a baseDir, but a library caller wouldn't know. Fewest elements: drop the no-baseDir mode, or report that the files were not checked.
findings.pull_quote: Without a folder the validator says yes to pictures that are not there, and says nothing about it.

findings.claim: The pointer warning's only negative case is the a.py:1 fixture. A brief citing templates/base.html:12 for a logic bug matches the regex at :353, and no test pins that boundary. The user cost is the product lenses' call. Mine: add one test so whatever gets ruled becomes the spec.
findings.pull_quote: The warning is tested on a mockup and on a .py file; where its boundary sits for a .html template is unwritten.
findings.need_info_reason: Whether a .html citation on a non-visual entry should warn is the deferred false-positive ruling.

findings.claim: On a phone nothing tells the reader a screenshot can be tapped. The only cues are cursor:zoom-in and a title tooltip, and touch shows neither. A tap widens the picture to true size with sideways scroll, while reference/diagrams.md:43 promises full size, so the documentation and the runtime disagree. The ruling already plans a fitted full-screen view. That fix should also add a visible cue (an icon or 'tap to enlarge') and a visible close control. Without them the reader cannot find the action or tell what state they are in.

evidence.note: cursors are the only state cue

findings.pull_quote: On a phone the screenshot looks like a plain picture: its only zoom cues are a hover cursor and a tooltip, so the reader can neither find the action nor see how to undo it.

findings.claim: The warning catches #46, but its idea of 'shown' is not the reader's. Any svg drawing silences it (line 349), so an entry whose evidence is a mockup path still passes if it carries an architecture svg. The pattern also fires on any .png, .svg or .html path and on the bare word screenshot or mockup (line 353), so a public brief about frontend assets gets flagged with no visual question in it. A warning that is often wrong teaches the agent author either to ignore it or to paste an irrelevant screenshot to quiet it. It also names .gif, which IMAGE_TYPES then refuses. Assumption: the false-positive rate is unknown.

evidence.note: any asset path or keyword matches
no frontend-asset negative case, no svg-silences case

findings.pull_quote: The warning treats any svg as shown and any asset path as visual: it misses the reader who still cannot see, and nags authors who were not asking a visual question.
findings.need_info_reason: False-positive rate is deferred; severity depends on it.

findings.claim: The over-1 MB refusal is a hard stop, and its hint (resize to 1600 px, re-encode as JPEG or WebP) needs an image tool that a session lacks. The recovery the author can reach goes unsaid: recapture at a narrower window or a cropped region with the browser tools (reference/diagrams.md:50-51). A remedy the author cannot carry out reads as a dead end. Assumption: no resize tool in session.
findings.pull_quote: The size refusal tells the author to resize or re-encode, which a session cannot do, and leaves out what it can do: retake the shot narrower or cropped.

findings.claim: Candidate, for an architecture spot-check. When extract skips a picture whose path climbs out of the folder, it warns but still reports the brief recovered. The next render refuses the whole page (render-brief.mjs:1155-1158), whereas an unreadable archify drawing degrades to a visible note (:212-213). Neither message names the other, so the person meets the failure two commands after its cause. Either the image should degrade the way archify does, or extract should say plainly that the brief will not render until the picture is re-attached.
findings.pull_quote: Extract skips a picture and reports success; the next render refuses the whole page. The cause and the failure sit two commands apart, and neither message names the other.

findings.claim: The page-weight budget has two authors, and neither one enforces the only limit that matters. The hard caps apply per file: 1 MB per picture in the validator and 4 MB per drawing in the renderer. Both totals only warn: picture bytes over 6 MB in the validator, the whole page over 6 MB in the renderer, and the validator's total leaves out inlined drawings. Thirteen pictures just under 1 MB embed to about 17 MB and pass both checks with warnings. The page then fails at publish, which defeats quality (a). Ruling: CONSOLIDATE the budget in validate-brief.mjs, which the renderer already imports, so this adds no new coupling. Count pictures and inlined drawings together, and refuse the estimated embedded size near 16 MB. Fitness function: a test where many sub-1 MB pictures over the ceiling are refused, and a check that the renderer holds no byte-limit constants of its own.

findings.claim: The page has two recovery contracts with different standing. The data block is declared stable: extract-brief.mjs:8-12 promises every page carries its data, and :29-30 keeps older pages readable. It has two readers. data-brief-file has no such declaration. findings.claim: The operator ruled this the wrong guard: what matters is intent to show, and a show must carry the representation. So the finding is no longer 'extract and tune the keyword heuristic'. Delete the regex over prose (validate-brief.mjs:348-357) and replace it with a structural rule keyed on a declared intent. When an entry or evidence item says the reader must see something, the validator requires an image (or svg) on it, as an error at raise/set. A rule over the data is testable at the edges and has no false-positive rate. A rule over wording has both problems, and the 'any svg counts' shortcut too.

findings.claim: The operator ruled that the guard should check intent to show, not wording, and that showing must contain the representation. The PR's guard guesses intent from words and paths (line 353), then accepts any svg as the representation (line 349). Both halves are wrong for the reader: it misses the #46 case whenever an unrelated svg is present, and it fires on ordinary code citations. The fix is to let the entry declare that the reader must see something, then require an image (or an svg of that very thing) on the entry or its evidence. Drop the keyword regex. data.disputed: Is the 1 MB per-picture cap a real obstacle? Richards (F3, now 🟢): this machine can resize, so the cap is reachable. Cooper (F5, 🟡): the author meets a hard stop whose hint names no tool, and the operator's question is never raised. Outcome differs: a refusal the author can act on, or a stop with no way forward.

Same cap, Norman's side. Richards (F3, now 🟢): resizing tools exist here. Norman (F12, 🟡): the refusal hint tells the author to resize, which public users may not be able to do, and leaves out retaking the shot narrower or cropped. Outcome differs: whether the message leads the author to a fix.

Where should the picture rule live? Richards (F4): keep render and extract copies of the img markup, pinned by the round-trip test. Uncle Bob (R2-4, F16): one function that validate, render and extract all call. No direct user-visible change; it sets how likely a later edit silently breaks recovering pictures.

Same question, Beck's side. Richards (F4): two copies are a sanctioned divergence, since extract importing the renderer would run its CLI. Beck (F21): the picture tag is one rule written twice; move it in a structure-only commit first. No direct user-visible change.

data.value: Closes the only attacker-reachable write: a page someone else published can no longer name a non-picture file (e.g. .claude/settings.json) for extract to write. Unblocks merge (🔴).
Pins the F1 fix with a test that goes red if the path and type refusals are removed, so the guard cannot silently regress. Unblocks merge (🔴).
Stops recovery from silently overwriting screenshots already beside the JSON; the operator's own files are never lost to a page. Unblocks merge (🔴).
Delivers the operator's ruling on the top-ranked quality: on a phone a tapped screenshot opens fitted in a full-screen view with pinch-zoom, instead of a true-size strip scrolled sideways.

Replaces the wording heuristic with the operator's rule (intent to show must carry the representation): fewer false warnings for public users, and the #46 case is caught per evidence item, not silenced by an unrelated svg.

tldr: Five lenses found PR #48 delivers screenshots inside the page, but the recovery step that writes pictures back from a published page trusts that page too far, the phone tap does the opposite of the operator's ruling, and the visual-pointer warning guards wording instead of intent.

The top five fix extract first (refuse non-picture and dot-segment names, never overwrite, with a hostile-page test), then fit-to-screen tap with full-screen pinch-zoom, then replace the keyword warning with a per-evidence rule that intent to show must carry the picture.
Three 🔴 findings block merge: F1 (extract writes any file a page names), F8 (extract silently overwrites existing pictures) and F15 (no test fails if the folder-escape refusal is removed).
